(AP Photo/Beata Zawrzel) FIFA President Gianni Infantino watched in Łódź, Poland as goalkeepr Laia López saved spot kicks from Choe Yon-a and Pak Il-Sim in the shootout after the game had ended 0-0. ŁÓDŹ Spain added to its burgeoning haul of global football titles after winning the Women’s Under-20 World Cup on Sunday. Goalkeeper Laia López saved two penalties in a 4-3 shootout win over defending champion North Korea in the final.

news.title: England 2-3 Spain: World champions win at Wembley in Nations League despite Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane goals
news.lede: Spain showed why they are the best national team in the world by emerging 3-2 winners from a thrilling, chaotic Nations League clash at Wembley, in which England's flaws undermined their exciting attacking play. It was the World Cup final that might have been had England not squandered their advantage against Argentina this summer - but Spain showed the gap in quality in a result which is a blow to Thomas Tuchel's stated aim of winning this competition. Bad errors from Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly helped Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena score Spain's first two and England were cut open through the match, including for Mikel Oyarzabal's winner which came with 16 minutes to play.

news.title: From the men to the young women: Spain tightens its grip on world football with a new title
news.lede: Spain were crowned champions of the FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup on Sunday, beating North Korea 4-3 on penalties after the final finished goalless. It's the second time Spain have lifted the trophy, having first won it in 2022. This time they stripped North Korea of the title the North Koreans had claimed in 2024. Two titles now make Spain the second most successful nation in the competition's history, trailing only the United States, Germany and North Korea, who each boast three.

news.title: Spain continue global football dominance with penalty shoot-out win against North Korea in U-20 World Cup final
news.lede: Match action and shoot-out dramaSpain have successfully claimed their second U-20 Women's World Cup title after an exhausting battle against North Korea today. The two sides could not be separated during normal time and extra time, resulting in a 0-0 draw. In the ensuing penalty shoot-out, Spain emerged victorious with a 4-3 win, largely thanks to heroic saves from goalkeeper Laia Lopez. North Korea, who secured the U-17 World Cup title against the Netherlands in 2025 with a dominant 3-0 victory, were ultimately unable to replicate that tournament-winning magic on this occasion.Breaking down a resilient defenceThroughout the 120 minutes, Spain dominated possession and continuously pressed the opposition, but they struggled to break down a resilient North Korean defence.
